Do you want to be a part of a dynamic team of highly motivated individuals who enjoy working to benefit present and future generations of Californians? Join the Delta Stewardship Council, where we ensure a more reliable California water supply and a resilient Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta ecosystem while protecting and enhancing the region as a special place where people live, work, and recreate!

In this position, you will perform scientific research that directly supports the Delta Independent Science Board's (Delta ISB) reviews of the scientific research, monitoring, and assessment programs that inform adaptive management of the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. Your research will involve literature reviews and syntheses obtained from workshops, interviews and surveys with the Delta community to help inform the recommendations of the Delta ISB on scientific issues important to management, including ecosystem restoration, water supply reliability, flood risk, water quality, and the Delta as an evolving place. As an Environmental Scientist, your expertise and research will help shape the next set of scientific reviews informing management decisions that affect the long-term health and resilience of the Delta.

Are you interested in a meaningful and impactful career? Would you like to contribute to protecting people and the environment and accelerating a statewide transition to sustainable pest management? The Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) could be the place for you!
  
  
Under the general direction of the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory), the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) serves as the supervisor for professional scientific staff within the Department of Pesticide Regulation’s (DPR) Pesticide Use Reporting (PUR) Program. This position plans, directs, and evaluates scientific, technical, and programmatic activities supporting the accuracy, completeness, accessibility, and effective use of statewide pesticide use data. The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) oversees PUR data quality and reporting activities, including quality assurance and quality control processes, development of the annual PUR report, responses to data requests, and technical support for urgent or complex data needs. The position provides technical and programmatic leadership on pesticide use reporting requirements, database and data system improvements, and changes resulting from legislation, regulation, and Department policy. The Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) supports implementation of Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Branch and Department priorities and follows direction and guidance provided by the Environmental Program Manager I (Supervisory), Branch Chief, and executive leadership.

jobs.description:
Grounded in safety, quality, and ethics, our experts lead their fields and guide our work with rigor, a creative spirit, and a vision for growth. We draw from more than 20 technical specialties worldwide and are committed to fostering an inclusive community of diverse talents, backgrounds, and expertise. We’re a place to apply your passion and collaborate with top environmental talents on work critical to our clients and the communities they support. Join a team that has the environment down to a science.

Your Opportunity

Stantec is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist to serve as a Planning Waters Team Lead for a large utility client within our environmental planning and natural resources practice. This position will provide technical and operational leadership for planning-related waters work, including jurisdictional waters and aquatic resources assessments, regulatory permitting, technical documentation, and environmental review.

The successful candidate will function as an experienced professional who applies advanced practical knowledge, exercises independent judgment, and resolves complex technical and project-delivery issues within established professional and regulatory practices. The role will also provide mentoring, work coordination, quality oversight, and technical direction to environmental scientists and other multidisciplinary team members.

Location

This role is based out of our Stantec office in San Diego, CA; however geographic alignment with other Stantec offices can be considered based on experience. Stantec offers flexible work locations (including working from home), flexible work hours, and a robust compensation and benefits package. Typical office environment working with computers and remaining sedentary for long periods of time.

Your Key Responsibilities

Provide technical and functional leadership for planning-related waters assignments, including aquatic resource evaluations, jurisdictional waters delineations, desktop assessments, field investigations, permitting, and environmental documentation.
Coordinate team workloads, assign or recommend assignments based on staff qualifications and availability, monitor schedules and deliverables, and identify resource needs or delivery risks.
Provide technical direction, coaching, mentoring, and quality-control support to junior and intermediate staff.
Develop regulatory strategies for projects requiring aquatic resource approvals or consultation.
Prepare and review permit applications and supporting materials associated with Clean Water Act Sections 404 and 401, Waste Discharge Requirements, and California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 Lake and Streambed Alteration Agreements, as applicable.
Prepare, review, and provide quality assurance and quality control for jurisdictional waters delineation reports, Aquatic Resources Delineation Reports, technical memoranda, biological resources reports, and permit packages.
Interpret federal, state, and local environmental requirements and advise project teams on applicable regulatory pathways, risks, data needs, and recommended next steps.
Coordinate with clients, project managers, technical specialists, and regulatory agencies regarding project requirements, technical findings, schedules, deliverables, and permitting strategies.
Lead or support agency coordination and negotiations, including responding to agency comments and requests for supplemental information.
Review work prepared by team members for technical accuracy, consistency, regulatory defensibility, completeness, and adherence to applicable quality standards.
Develop and improve team procedures, templates, quality-control tools, technical guidance, and training materials to support consistent project delivery.
Lead by example in applying Stantec and client health, safety, security, and environmental requirements.

Your Capabilities and Credentials

Advanced practical knowledge of aquatic resources, jurisdictional waters, wetlands, streams, riparian systems, and related environmental planning and permitting requirements.
Working knowledge of the Clean Water Act, including Sections 404 and 401; applicable state water-quality requirements; Waste Discharge Requirements; and California Fish and Game Code Section 1600 requirements.
Experience developing aquatic resource permitting strategies and preparing or reviewing permit applications and supporting technical documentation.
Ability to independently evaluate complex technical and regulatory issues, interpret available information, and recommend practical, defensible solutions.
Demonstrated ability to lead technical workstreams, coordinate workloads, guide teams, and deliver assignments within established scope, budget, schedule, and quality expectations.
Experience mentoring staff, reviewing technical work, providing constructive feedback, and supporting employee development.
Strong technical writing, editing, verbal communication, presentation, and organizational skills.
Ability to communicate technical information clearly to clients, project managers, multidisciplinary teams, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
Ability to build productive professional relationships and work collaboratively across offices, disciplines, and business lines.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to technically accurate, complete, and high-quality deliverables.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and Adobe Acrobat.
Must have valid driver's license and clean MVR

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, biology, ecology, wetland science, natural resources, soil science, botany, environmental planning, or a related discipline.

Minimum of five years of directly related professional experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Experience successfully leading the technical aspects of small to medium projects or significant workstreams within larger, multidisciplinary projects.

Experience supporting utility, energy, transportation, infrastructure, restoration, or land-development projects is preferred.

and Environment Protection Regulations 2020. Investigate, develop and implement environmental protection policies, guidance and
  
strategies related to such development.

Protection Authority (NT EPA) and prepares Ministerial environmental approvals under the EP Act.

1. Identify, critically analyse and assess risks and potential environmental impacts associated with development proposals and make

recommendations on the level of environmental assessment, environmental protection safeguards and standards that should be
  
incorporated in conditions of approval consistent with best practice environmental management.

development matters that come under the responsibility of the Environmental Assessment Unit.

ensure that advice and recommendations for environmental protection are accurately translated into conditions of approval for
  
development proposals.

proposals based on advice and recommendations for environmental approval.

industry and consultants about development proposals and the environmental impact assessment process.

6. Prepare documents to support implementation of environmental impact assessment processes including guidance, procedures and
  
policies.

7. Mentor and support staff when required.

range of stakeholders.

5. Demonstrated negotiation and problem solving skills, initiative, flexibility and ability to effectively manage conflict.
  
6. Well-developed research, investigative and analytical abilities to interpret technical and complex information and prepare professional

reports, policies, strategies and guidance material.

1. Knowledge of legislation related to environment protection or environmental impact assessment.
  
2. Technical experience in the assessment of impacts on the biophysical (water quality, air quality, ecosystems), social and/or cultural

aspects of the environment, including knowledge of applying regulatory standards.

**The Position**
----------------

Under direct or general supervision, performs a variety of technical to complex monitoring inspection, and compliance in the administration of the Certified Unified Program Agency (CUPA), which implements hazardous materials business plan, hazardous waste generators, onsite hazardous waste treatment, underground storage tanks, Aboveground Petroleum Storage (APSA), and California Accidental Release Prevention Program (CalARP) programs; identifies violations of codes and regulations, ;conducts field inspections; collects and records data; prepares reports; maintains a variety of records and files; and performs related duties as assigned.
  
  
**Distinguishing Characteristics**
  
***Hazardous Materials Specialist I****:* This is the entry-level classification in the Hazardous Materials Specialist series. Initially under close supervision, incumbents with basic experience learn City systems, operations, practices, and procedures. As experience is gained, assignments become more varied, complex, and difficult; close supervision and frequent review of work lessen as an incumbent demonstrates skill to perform the work independently. Positions at this level usually perform most of the duties required of the positions at the Hazardous Materials Specialist II-level but are not expected to function at the same skill level and usually exercise less independent discretion and judgment in matters related to work procedures and methods. Work is usually supervised while in progress and fits an established structure or pattern. Exceptions or changes in procedures are explained in detail as they arise.
  
  
***Hazardous Materials Specialist II****:* This is the journey-level classification in the Hazardous Materials Specialist series. Positions at this level are distinguished from the Hazardous Materials Specialist I-level by the performance of the full range of duties as assigned, working independently, and exercising judgment and initiative. Positions at this level receive only occasional instruction or assistance as new or unusual situations arise and are fully aware of the operating procedures and policies of the work unit.
  
  
Positions in the Hazardous Materials Specialist class series are flexibly staffed; positions at the Hazardous Materials Specialist II-level are normally filled by advancement from the Hazardous Materials Specialist I-level; progression to the Hazardous Materials Specialist II-level is dependent on (i) management affirmation that the position is performing the full range of duties assigned to the classification; (ii) satisfactory work performance; (iii) the incumbent meeting the minimum qualifications for the classification including any licenses and certifications; and (iv) management approval for progression to the Hazardous Materials Specialist II-level.
  
  
**Supervision Exercised and Received**:
  
Receives direct supervision (Hazardous Materials Specialist I) or general supervision (Hazardous Materials Specialist II) from the Hazardous Materials Supervisor. Exercises no direct supervision over staff.

**Duties and Responsibilities**
-------------------------------

*The typical job functions of the classification may include, but are not limited to, the functions below and are subject to changes in operational necessity.*
  
*Positions at the I-level may perform some of these duties and responsibilities in a learning capacity.*

* Performs routine and non-routine inspections and associated technical tasks in the administration and implementation of the City’s Certified Unified Program Agency (CUPA) program which include: Aboveground Petroleum Storage Act (APSA); Area Plans for hazardous materials emergencies; California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) for extremely hazardous substances, including toxic and flammable materials; Hazardous Materials Business Plans for onsite handling of hazardous materials; Hazardous Waste/Universal Waste Generator and Onsite Hazardous Waste Treatment; and Underground Storage Tanks.
* Responds to and investigates inquiries/complaints and agency referrals related to the handling, storage, or disposal of hazardous materials .
* Communicates with facility representatives about regulatory violations, enforcement actions, waste minimization and industrial and commercial stormwater controls..
* Reviews Risk Management Plans and inspects and audits industrial facilities covered under the California Accidental Release Program.
* Reviews Hazardous Materials Business Plans and Hazardous Waste Generator Registrations submitted through the California Environmental Reporting System (CERS) for completeness, accuracy, and compliance with applicable state and federal codes and regulations.
* Conducts plan reviews for new construction/alteration to ensure compliance with applicable codes and regulations including the hazardous materials provisions of the California Fire Code.
* Permits, inspects, and oversees the installation and removal of underground hazardous materials storage tank systems.
* Perform related duties as required.

**Education**: Educational requirements as specified in **California Code of Regulations, Title 27 §15260****.** Equivalent to graduation from an accredited college or university or equivalent degree with major course work in one of the following disciplines of biology or microbiology, chemistry, chemical engineering, physics, physical science, environment science, geology or soil science, environmental health, environmental or sanitary engineering, toxicology, industrial hygiene, hazardous materials management, fire science or fire technology.

### **Job Description and Duties**

The incumbent supports comprehensive habitat management and wildlife conservation activities on the Grizzly Island Wildlife Area (GIWA). Duties include conducting wildlife surveys to assess species inventory, status, habitat use, production, population trends, and distribution. The position monitors wildlife populations associated with federal and State requirements, including the Federal Assistance (Pittman-Robertson) grant and listed species obligations. The incumbent coordinates with agencies, conservation groups, private landowners, and researchers to access lands and complete resource assessments, providing written reports to guide management actions.

  

Wildlife habitat management: The incumbent assists with mowing, noxious weed control, species eradication efforts, and the operation of water delivery systems to apply water for flood and irrigation cycles that support wetland habitat and benefit target wildlife species. The position provides biological expertise and best management practices for Suisun Marsh projects related to wildlife, vegetation, water, and threatened and endangered species. The incumbent develops geographic information system (GIS)/global positioning system (GPS) maps for habitat projects, vegetation, invasive species, public uses, and maintains digital resource data for the wildlife area. The role includes leading the creation and updating of Land Management Plans and representing CDFW in meetings related to land use, project development, and resource issues.

Hunting recreation: Includes coordinating regulations, guidelines, and hunter quotas; conducting elk hunter orientations and hunts; collecting biological samples from harvested game, assisting the Game Bird Heritage and Waterfowl Program with special hunt opportunities such as Junior Pheasant hunts; supporting waterfowl check station operations. Under the direction of the Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisor, the incumbent will serve as one of the lead field scientists for the Nutria Eradication Program. This position will play a critical role in the coordination of field crews conducting nutria surveys and trapping across the southern portion of the nutria infestation. VENTURA COUNTY

The County's 1,873 square miles include 1,846 square miles of land with 42 miles of coastline which is home to the following cities and points of interest: Camarillo, Fillmore, Moorpark, Ojai, Oxnard, Port Hueneme, Santa Paula, Simi Valley, Thousand Oaks, and Ventura as well as national protected areas such as parts of the Angeles National Forest, Channel Islands National Park, and the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area.

Ventura County is a “general law” county, governed by a five-member, elected-by-district Board of Supervisors. RMA includes five divisions: Environmental Health, Planning, Building &Safety, Code Compliance, and Operations/GIS.

The key responsibility of the Environmental Health Division is to protect public health and the environment by ensuring conformance with State laws and County ordinances pertaining to the following programs: food protection, hazardous materials, hazardous waste, individual sewage disposal systems, land use, medical waste, ocean water quality monitoring, recreational health, solid waste, underground fuel tanks, and vector control.

Those at the Environmental Health Specialist IV level may act as project team leaders and program coordinators. Each succeeding step in the job series is expected to function at a higher level of individual initiative, creativity, self-direction, and independent judgment.

Lead and grow a strategic environmental assessment and remediation practice in California, with a focus on Fresno, the Central Valley, and Northern California.

Serve as a Client Manager, Account Lead, or senior technical advisor for key strategic clients.
